raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-PER-ArequipaColca",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "GORE Arequipa and the PIU lack experience with World Bank-financed operations, risking non-compliance with fiduciary, procurement, and environmental/social requirements.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Provide targeted FM and procurement training, appoint qualified PIU key staff early, and utilize GFPP grant funding for capacity building prior to effectiveness.",
      "evidence": "Given the lack of experience of the PIU with World Bank or other multilateral-financed projects, targeted capacity building and training... will be required."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Institutional fragmentation across line ministries, regional, and municipal governments may impede effective coordination across the 33 multi-sectoral sub-investments.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish a high-level Steering Committee and Consultative Committee, and execute Interinstitutional Agreements with all participating municipalities.",
      "evidence": "Efficient budgeting and implementation of investments in tourism are hindered by lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Severe climate events such as extreme rainfall, flooding, and landslides could damage rural transport infrastructure and disrupt access to tourism corridors.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Design roads with climate-resilient engineering standards, including slope stabilization, enhanced drainage systems, properly sized culverts, and rapid assistance emergency response plans.",
      "evidence": "floods and resulting mudslides weaken transportation infrastructure, road closures impede access to tourism destinations, particularly those most isolated"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "High regional seismic activity poses a threat of structural damage or collapse to 17th–19th century historical churches and heritage sites during or post-rehabilitation.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply traditional resilient restoration techniques, structural reinforcement, and prepare risk management manuals with staff training.",
      "evidence": "The churches were built in the 17th to 19th centuries and are in various states of disrepair, many having suffered earthquake damage."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Initial project execution may face budget allocation and budget execution delays within Peru's public finance system, impairing timely disbursement.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "GORE Arequipa will initiate budget allocation procedures for external and local resources immediately upon loan signing as specified in the POM.",
      "evidence": "In Peru, initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates, which could affect project readiness"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Disbursement for main infrastructure components depends on executing mandatory Interinstitutional Agreements, risking implementation schedule slippage.",
      "category": "schedule",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Accelerate drafting and signing of Interinstitutional Agreements and POM adoption using pre-effective GFPP grant support.",
      "evidence": "No withdrawals shall be made for Goods, works... for Parts/components 1 and 2... until and unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "High baseline road fatality rates in Arequipa could lead to increased traffic accidents as tourist traffic grows along improved road corridors.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate road safety features like guardrails, signage, pedestrian crossings, speed calming, and conduct mandatory road safety audits.",
      "evidence": "In 2024, Arequipa recorded 11.7 road traffic deaths per 100,000 people, a significantly higher rate than Peru's national average of 8.8"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Inadequate long-term funding and capacity for operation and maintenance (O&M) could lead to rapid degradation of upgraded transport, water, and tourism infrastructure.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Establish explicit O&M funding mechanisms, formal asset transfer agreements, and O&M capacity-building plans for local management entities.",
      "evidence": "Destination management and governance also exhibit large capacity and funding gaps and limited coordination between public and private stakeholders."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Inexperience with World Bank financial management standards may cause financial record errors or delays in audit compliance.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Utilize the SIAF national accounting system, mandate annual independent financial audits, and define detailed key FM controls in the POM.",
      "evidence": "Inadequate experience with Bank-financed projects may result in errors in financial records and reporting."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Female workers face entry barriers, persistent wage gaps, and potential risks of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEA/SH) in project activities.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement a project SEA/SH Action Plan, deliver targeted capacity building through women's organizations, and design gender-informed infrastructure.",
      "evidence": "women’s participation in tourism is lower than potential, and women are exposed to a gender wage gap, leaving them more exposed to income insecurity."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Unaddressed local community concerns or delayed grievance resolution could generate local social opposition to infrastructure sub-projects.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and establish a functional Project-level Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) to track and resolve grievances.",
      "evidence": "percentage of project-related grievances addressed by the PIU, through the application of the project-level grievance mechanism"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "High labor informality and lack of granular local labor data create technical challenges in accurately tracking project employment outcomes.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 2,
      "mitigation": "Leverage innovative remote sensing methodologies, satellite imagery, AI algorithms, and dedicated tourism observatory surveys.",
      "evidence": "Measuring the impact of project interventions on jobs is difficult considering the high level of informality, the lack of monitoring of jobs at a granular level"
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: GORE Arequipa and the PIU lack experience with World Bank-financed operations, risking non-compliance with fiduciary, procurement, and environmental/social requirements.
risks.mitigation: Provide targeted FM and procurement training, appoint qualified PIU key staff early, and utilize GFPP grant funding for capacity building prior to effectiveness.
risks.evidence: Given the lack of experience of the PIU with World Bank or other multilateral-financed projects, targeted capacity building and training... will be required.

risks.description: Institutional fragmentation across line ministries, regional, and municipal governments may impede effective coordination across the 33 multi-sectoral sub-investments.
risks.mitigation: Establish a high-level Steering Committee and Consultative Committee, and execute Interinstitutional Agreements with all participating municipalities.
risks.evidence: Efficient budgeting and implementation of investments in tourism are hindered by lack of coordination within a highly fragmented institutional landscape

risks.description: Severe climate events such as extreme rainfall, flooding, and landslides could damage rural transport infrastructure and disrupt access to tourism corridors.
risks.mitigation: Design roads with climate-resilient engineering standards, including slope stabilization, enhanced drainage systems, properly sized culverts, and rapid assistance emergency response plans.
risks.evidence: floods and resulting mudslides weaken transportation infrastructure, road closures impede access to tourism destinations, particularly those most isolated

risks.description: High regional seismic activity poses a threat of structural damage or collapse to 17th–19th century historical churches and heritage sites during or post-rehabilitation.
risks.mitigation: Apply traditional resilient restoration techniques, structural reinforcement, and prepare risk management manuals with staff training.
risks.evidence: The churches were built in the 17th to 19th centuries and are in various states of disrepair, many having suffered earthquake damage.

risks.description: Initial project execution may face budget allocation and budget execution delays within Peru's public finance system, impairing timely disbursement.
risks.mitigation: GORE Arequipa will initiate budget allocation procedures for external and local resources immediately upon loan signing as specified in the POM.
risks.evidence: In Peru, initial project implementation phases often experience delays in budget allocation and low budget execution rates, which could affect project readiness

risks.description: Disbursement for main infrastructure components depends on executing mandatory Interinstitutional Agreements, risking implementation schedule slippage.
risks.mitigation: Accelerate drafting and signing of Interinstitutional Agreements and POM adoption using pre-effective GFPP grant support.
risks.evidence: No withdrawals shall be made for Goods, works... for Parts/components 1 and 2... until and unless the Bank has received at least three signed Interinstitutional Agreements

risks.description: High baseline road fatality rates in Arequipa could lead to increased traffic accidents as tourist traffic grows along improved road corridors.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate road safety features like guardrails, signage, pedestrian crossings, speed calming, and conduct mandatory road safety audits.
risks.evidence: In 2024, Arequipa recorded 11.7 road traffic deaths per 100,000 people, a significantly higher rate than Peru's national average of 8.8

risks.description: Inadequate long-term funding and capacity for operation and maintenance (O&M) could lead to rapid degradation of upgraded transport, water, and tourism infrastructure.
risks.mitigation: Establish explicit O&M funding mechanisms, formal asset transfer agreements, and O&M capacity-building plans for local management entities.
risks.evidence: Destination management and governance also exhibit large capacity and funding gaps and limited coordination between public and private stakeholders.

risks.description: Inexperience with World Bank financial management standards may cause financial record errors or delays in audit compliance.
risks.mitigation: Utilize the SIAF national accounting system, mandate annual independent financial audits, and define detailed key FM controls in the POM.
risks.evidence: Inadequate experience with Bank-financed projects may result in errors in financial records and reporting.

risks.description: Female workers face entry barriers, persistent wage gaps, and potential risks of sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEA/SH) in project activities.
risks.mitigation: Implement a project SEA/SH Action Plan, deliver targeted capacity building through women's organizations, and design gender-informed infrastructure.
risks.evidence: women’s participation in tourism is lower than potential, and women are exposed to a gender wage gap, leaving them more exposed to income insecurity.

risks.description: Unaddressed local community concerns or delayed grievance resolution could generate local social opposition to infrastructure sub-projects.
risks.mitigation: Implement the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP) and establish a functional Project-level Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM) to track and resolve grievances.
risks.evidence: percentage of project-related grievances addressed by the PIU, through the application of the project-level grievance mechanism

risks.description: High labor informality and lack of granular local labor data create technical challenges in accurately tracking project employment outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Leverage innovative remote sensing methodologies, satellite imagery, AI algorithms, and dedicated tourism observatory surveys.
risks.evidence: Measuring the impact of project interventions on jobs is difficult considering the high level of informality, the lack of monitoring of jobs at a granular level
